attentionCallout.label: Attention required
attentionCallout.description: Processing prepares a resource for search — only ready resources can be cited as sources in projects and theological queries.

extracting.label: In progress
extracting.description: This can take several minutes depending on the document's size and complexity. No action needed — indexing runs automatically once extraction finishes.

failed.label: Extraction failed
failed.description: Something failed while processing the file. Check each affected resource below and either delete or re-upload it.

indexFailed.label: Indexing failed
indexFailed.description: The text extracted fine, but building the search index failed, so these resources can't be searched or cited yet. Retrying doesn't use up any of your page balance.

upload.modeStandardDescription: Narrative books, essays and sermons (up to ~600 pages). Consumes standard pages.
upload.modePremiumDescription: Tables, multi-column and scanned (up to ~1000 pages). Consumes premium pages.
upload.tierCalloutPremiumOnly: This file ({{sizeMB}}MB) exceeds the Premium limit ({{premiumCapMB}}MB). Premium is disabled; Standard will be used.
upload.tierCalloutStandardOnly: This file ({{sizeMB}}MB) exceeds the Standard limit ({{standardCapMB}}MB). Standard is disabled; Premium still handles it.
upload.tierCalloutBoth: This file ({{sizeMB}}MB) exceeds the Premium ({{premiumCapMB}}MB) and Standard ({{standardCapMB}}MB) limits. It will be processed with Basic (free, reduced quality).

modeAdvice.scan-fits-vision: This is a scan: its pages are images. Standard runs them through vision and recovers the text; Premium rebuilds layout over text that already exists, and on a scan it returns garbage.
modeAdvice.scan-too-large: This is a scan over 50 MB, so it does not fit vision. No route works: Standard would fall back to reading a text layer that a scan does not have, and Premium destroys non-Latin script. Split the file before uploading.
modeAdvice.text-layer-premium: It has a text layer. Premium rebuilds tables and columns; Standard is enough for running prose.
modeAdvice.over-every-cap: Over 100 MB — no engine accepts it. Split it into volumes before uploading.

upload.stepModeWaiting: Pick the file first — the right route depends on what it is.

metadataBackfill.body: We can infer the books from the title (BHQ → whole OT, "2 Peter & Jude" → 2 Peter + Jude, etc.) and fill them in automatically. We only write when the match is clear; the rest you can edit manually.

summary.manual_one: {{count}} without a confident match — edit manually from the resource.
summary.manual_other: {{count}} without a confident match — edit manually from each resource.
summary.manualWithFailures: {{manual}} without a confident match. {{failed}} save errors — try again.

toast.allSkipped: No title had enough signal to infer books automatically

toast.cancelTooLate: Already finished processing — use Delete instead of Cancel
toast.processWarning: No fragments generated for "{{title}}". The text may be unreadable or too short.
toast.textNotReady: The text is still being extracted. Wait a few seconds and try again.
toast.reprocessConfirm: Reprocess "{{title}}"? Existing fragments will be deleted and regenerated.
toast.reprocessWarning: No new fragments generated during reprocessing
toast.processingComplete: Processing completed with {{count}} errors. {{chunks}} fragments created.
toast.retryPremiumNoBalance: You don't have enough Premium pages to retry
toast.retryPremiumDenied: You can only retry your own resources

toast.retryIndexingError_other: Couldn't index {{count}} resources. Try again in a few minutes.

citedResourceMissing: The source you cited is no longer in your library. You may have deleted it after preparing that sermon.

preflight.measured: Measured on your device across {{pages}} pages, without uploading anything.
preflight.measuredDetail: Sample: pages {{from}} to {{to}} · {{chars}} characters of text found.

apto.title: The file looks good
apto.body: It carries its text inside, so Preach will be able to search and cite within this book — including Greek or Hebrew words with their accents.

sin-capa-de-texto.title: This file is photos of the pages, not text
sin-capa-de-texto.body: It reads fine, but inside there are no letters — only images. Preach won't be able to search inside it or cite from it. If you have another version of the same book, try that one. You can upload it anyway, but it will likely end up unusable.

escritura-ausente.title: This file's text is damaged
escritura-ausente.body: It reads fine on screen, but the letters stored inside are not the ones it displays. Whatever reaches Preach will be gibberish, impossible to search or cite. Look for another version of this book before uploading.

escritura-sin-diacriticos.title: The Greek or Hebrew comes without its accents
escritura-sin-diacriticos.body: The book is fine to read, but searching for a Greek or Hebrew word with its accents won't find it, because this file lost them. Upload it if reading is enough; for original-language study another version is better.

sin-escritura-original.title: We found no Greek or Hebrew inside
sin-escritura-original.body: If this book doesn't use them, it's perfectly fine. If it's a grammar, a critical text or a technical commentary that should carry them, then this file lost them and they would arrive unreadable.

numbering.title: Book page numbering
numbering.loadFailed: Could not read this resource's sheet index.
numbering.previewTitle: This is how it will be saved
numbering.previewEmpty: Fill in at least one sheet to see the ranges.
numbering.uncalibratedHint: Citations from this resource will say “sheet N” until you confirm its numbering.
numbering.pageIntro: Look at each sheet and tell us the number printed on it, usually at the foot. With that, citations from this book can say “p. 28” instead of “sheet 32”.
numbering.alreadyConfirmed: You already confirmed this book's numbering. You can correct it.
numbering.printedQuestion: What number is printed on sheet {{sheet}}?
numbering.lookForFolio: The folio is usually at the foot, sometimes in the header. It may be arabic or roman — type it as printed. If this sheet doesn't show it, check the next one rather than marking it as unnumbered.
numbering.unnumberedHint: Only tick this when the page carries no printed number at all, such as a plate or a blank leaf. If it has a roman numeral, type it: «ccxxii» is as citable a page as 222.
numbering.frontMatter: the first {{count}} sheets fall in the front matter
numbering.missingSteps_one: Sheet {{sheets}} is still unanswered. Type its printed number or mark it as unnumbered.
numbering.missingSteps_other: Sheets {{sheets}} are still unanswered. Type their printed numbers or mark them as unnumbered.
numbering.nothingToSave: No sheet has been answered yet.

calibrationCallout.title: {{count}} resource(s) without confirmed page numbering
calibrationCallout.body: Until you say which number each sheet carries in print, their citations will read «sheet N» — a number from the file that does not exist in the printed copy, and that nobody can check.
